title: A typed shipment manifest
objective: Connect the tool set to a small typed UI.
tasks: Add a required priority union (standard | express) to Shipment; make S-101 express and the others standard.
Calculate total pallets and the number of ready shipments from the array.
Render each shipment’s priority next to its status.
hints: Edit /shipments.ts first; TypeScript points out every missing priority.
Use reduce for the pallet sum and filter for ready shipments.

title: React state and events
objective: Connect events, state updates, and accessible feedback.
tasks: Wire Remove pallet to a functional state update that never goes below zero.
Disable Remove pallet when the count is zero.
Wire Reset to restore zero; check add, remove, and reset in the preview.
hints: Use setCount(current => ...) when the new value depends on the previous one.
Use Math.max(0, current - 1) and the native disabled prop.

title: A bounded MobX collection
objective: Use observable data, computed values, and actions with observer.
tasks: Implement total as a computed getter that sums all counter values.
Clamp every change to the inclusive range -10 through 10, even for ±100.
Limit the collection to three counters. Remove one and confirm a new counter can be added.
hints: makeAutoObservable infers observable fields, computed getters, and actions; autoBind keeps method callbacks safe.
Keep the observer wrapper: it subscribes the rendered collection and total to MobX changes.

title: Two views of the shipping board
objective: Derive a filtered table and ramp overview from the same local data.
tasks: Filter loadings by the selected status; All must restore all three rows.
In Ramps view, group the filtered loadings by rampId and show each ramp’s name.
Keep empty ramps visible with a no-matching-loadings message; preserve the filter when switching views.
hints: Derive visible from filter; do not store a second copy of the loading array in state.
Map over ramps, then filter visible for each ramp.id. R3 intentionally has no assignments.

title: Write CounterStore tests
objective: Turn manual observations into isolated, repeatable Vitest assertions.
tasks: Complete the addition/subtraction test: after the existing +4 assertion, apply -2 and assert 2.
Test upper and lower clamping, including another change at each boundary.
Test reset after a nonzero value and prove that separate store instances do not share state.
Run pnpm exec vitest run in the exported project; all five tests must pass with none pending.
hints: Create fresh stores inside each it block so tests do not depend on execution order.
Assert exact values before and after reset. A test that only constructs a store does not prove its behavior.

title: Fetch with cleanup and retry
objective: Load a local fixture safely, report failures, and retry without reloading the page.
tasks: In loadRamps, check response.ok before parsing JSON and throw an error containing the HTTP status.
Create an AbortController per effect, pass its signal to loadLocalRamps, and abort during cleanup; keep the active guard to ignore stale completions.
Wire Retry request to a request counter in the effect dependencies so the same URL is fetched again.
Check the success, loading, and error states; toggle the missing fixture, retry it, then restore the working fixture.
hints: The provided loadLocalRamps adapter tries /ramps.json for Vite and falls back to /public/ramps.json for Sandpack’s static-file service worker. Keep the fixture in /public.
A Vite dev server may return HTML with status 200 for a missing URL; JSON parsing still rejects and must reach the error UI.
Cleanup must mark the effect inactive before aborting, so intentional cancellation does not show an error.

title: UI5 shipment progress
objective: Compose ThemeProvider, Button, registered icons, and ProgressIndicator.
tasks: Convert the loaded pallet count into a 0–100 progress percentage (one pallet means 10%).
Clamp Load pallet to ten and disable it at capacity.
Wire Reset shipment to zero; verify the progress and action state reset together.
hints: Keep ThemeProvider around the app and use the UI5 v2 value and displayValue props.
UI5 v2 icon registration uses @ui5/webcomponents-icons/dist/add.js and refresh.js; Button takes the registered name.
